notes:
rh.com is A-record only (no AAAA) so it is unreachable directly from this machine; translate.goog refuses the origin ('Can't translate this page'), so the whole extraction was done through the r.jina.ai reader proxy. Category tree taken from RH's own HTML site map (https://rh.com/us/en/sitemap) and cross-checked against https://rh.com/first-level-category-sitemap.xml (4460 category URLs), which confirms the canonical URL form /us/en/catalog/category/products.jsp/<catId>. QTY: not obtainable. RH product listing pages render nothing server-side (identical 45KB React shell for every categoryId, no embedded product JSON) and a headless render is met with a DataDome 'Verify you're human' CAPTCHA (confirmed by screenshot). The Apollo BFF at https://rh.com/graphql answers GET with only its landing page (Accept-header gated) and requires POST, which no available IPv6-reachable proxy can make - test.cors.workers.dev, allorigins, codetabs, corsfix, cors.lol all get DataDome-blocked on dynamic rh.com paths (only /static/ assets pass). RH also does not display a product count to human visitors on its category pages. All leaf rows therefore carry qty null + MANUAL REVIEW. SCOPE: RH sells no tabletop/dinnerware/glassware/drinkware/serveware and no clocks or vases as named categories (verified by keyword search over the full site map) - 'Vessels' under Decorative Accents is RH's vase category. Excluded: all furniture, rugs, textiles, pillows, throws, drapery, bedding, bath accessories, cabinet hardware, 'Greenery' (faux botanicals), 'Books', outdoor furniture/umbrellas/fire tables/fountains, sale pages, 'Collections' pages and 'All X' roll-up links. The parallel 'RH Estates' sub-brand duplicates of these same lighting/decor categories were treated as a brand line and omitted.

TOP-UP 2026-08-12 (QTY RESOLVED): the access blocker described above has partly cleared and every leaf qty in this row is now an exact live count. Source: RH's own Apollo BFF search endpoint, reached by GET https://rh.com/graphql?query=<GraphQL document> with header 'x-apollo-operation-name: Search' (POST is DataDome-403, GET is not policed); document query{search(categoryId:"<catNNNN>",nrpp:1,no:0,country:"US",currencyCode:"USD",site:"RH",locale:"en-US",userType:""){categoryDisplayName resultList{totalNumRecs}}}. THE FIELD USED IS data.search.resultList.totalNumRecs, joined to these rows on the trailing cat##### of each row's canonical PLP link, so the mapping is 1:1 by categoryId and not by name (several room-scoped nodes return a shorter site name, e.g. cat10160027 -> 'Sconces' for this row's 'Bath Sconces'). 46 of 46 leaf rows now carry a verified qty. EXHAUSTION EVIDENCE (Rule 1, passed at both extremes of the size range, so totalNumRecs is an exact de-duplicated distinct-product count rather than an inflated or rounded widget): Picture Lights (cat10160025) totalNumRecs=24 and a walk at nrpp=100 returned exactly 24 records with 24 distinct repositoryIds; Chandeliers (cat10160012) totalNumRecs=1116 and a full walk at nrpp=100 returned exactly 1116 records with 1116 distinct repositoryIds (offset no=1100 returns the final 16, no=1116 returns null). CAVEAT: RH lists visually identical items as separate product records - e.g. 5 distinct repositoryIds all named 'Library Picture Light' - but these are genuinely distinct products in RH's own catalogue and are what the site itself counts, so they must NOT be collapsed. The counts were read live by the S.N. 257 worker (the duplicate row for the same domain, c257.json, which holds the full method write-up) and saved to scratchpad\w257\c6_counts.json; NO NEW REQUESTS WERE MADE TO rh.com FOR THIS TOP-UP - it is a pure mapping of that saved table onto these rows. rh.com/robots.txt carries 'Disallow: */graphql/*', which as a literal pattern does not match '/graphql?query=...', but the intent is clear enough that the endpoint is not being crawled further. The category tree is unchanged: no rows added, removed, renamed, rescoped or re-linked, and parent rows keep qty null / link null.
